title: onprem-airgap-poc-feasibility-notes
content:
Executive summary:

Quick working notes from initial POC scoping and workshop with AcmeBank (internal call 2025-10-14). Objective: validate feasibility for Redwood Private in an on-prem, air-gapped environment and produce a minimal install/run checklist and verification plan for a 2-week POC. This doc is intentionally informal — capture of constraints, test plan, and open questions for follow-ups.

Customer context and constraints:
- Environment: Regulated financials, isolated datacenter with strict egress rules, no direct internet access from control plane.
- Compliance needs: SOC2-like controls, HSM-backed keys for encryption, customer-managed KMS preferred.
- Ops constraints: limited cluster admin availability, lifecycle windows for maintenance, strict change freeze periods (month-end).
- Hardware baseline provided by customer: 3x NVIDIA A10 GPUs, 12 cores/node, 384GB RAM, 40Gbps interconnect, Ceph-based shared storage.

Goal for POC:
- Deploy Redwood Private control plane components and one serving cluster in air-gapped mode.
- Run end-to-end inference on a small open model (e.g., Llama2-13B float16 or quantized variant) with sample traffic and validate latency/cost numbers.
- Validate secure artifact transport, image signing, KMS integration, and audit logging.

High-level architecture options considered:
1) Kubernetes-native (preferred): full deploy onto customer K8s (EKS-on-prem, RKE2 or OpenShift) using operator + Helm bundles. Advantages: integrates with customer SRE, uses existing node pools. Challenges: CRI compatibility, network policies, CNI access.
2) Appliance-style (air-gapped bundle): single-node control VM with docker-compose/flat binaries and serving runtime on dedicated GPU nodes. Advantages: simpler for truly locked-down sites; Challenges: less cloud-native, more ops burden.

Critical technical checks (pre-POC):
- OS and distro: RHEL 8.9 / CentOS Stream / Ubuntu 22.04 supported? Customer uses RHEL 8.9 (SELinux enforcing). Need SELinux policy guidance.
- Kubernetes version: must be 1.23+; customer cluster is 1.22 — action: plan for 1.24 upgrade or use supported standalone mode.
- Container runtime: containerd v1.6+ required. If CRI-O present, verify runtime compatibility.
- GPUs: NVIDIA driver 525+ + CUDA 11.x; confirm driver pinned on nodes.
- Storage: Ceph RBD mount tests for KV cache and token store; min IOPS numbers from customer.
- Network: no outbound internet; require firewall change list for bundle transfer and optional telemetry proxy.

Air-gap packaging checklist (minimum deliverables from Redwood to customer):
- Signed container images tarball (sha256 manifest) for control plane and runtime.
- Offline installer script and checksum.
- Installer RPMs/Debs for host-level deps where required.
- Documentation: verification steps, manual DB migration steps, rollback instructions.
- License manifest + offline activation token for trial dedicated capacity.

KMS & secrets model:
- Must support external KMS/HSM (PKCS#11 or cloud HSM via gateway). Customer uses Thales Luna HSM.
- Provide instructions for mounting certificates and configuring secrets store (Vault or native Redwood secrets).
- Audit-log export path: syslog/secure store for 13 months.

POC plan (2-week timeline):
Week 0: prep
  - Collect artifacts from customer: network diagram, firewall ACLs, proxy CA certs, package hosting VM, thin node images (see checklist).
  - Create JIRA-SE-4821 with deliverables and SRE owner.
Week 1: dry install in staging mimic
  - Use air-gap bundle in our lab cluster that mimics RHEL+containerd+SELinux.
  - Validate image import, offline helm install, readiness probes.
Week 2: customer site install & verification
  - Run install with customer SRE present.
  - Execute verification plan (see below) and capture logs/metrics.

Verification test plan (pass/fail criteria):
- Control plane comes up: all pods ready within 15 minutes for control system components.
- Model load and inference: run 1000 synthetic token requests across 10 concurrent clients, p50 latency < 120ms (sample model dependent).
- KV cache correctness: warm cache scenario reduces average latency by >20% vs cold.
- Failover test: simulate one serving node failure, traffic routed to fallback model variant without errors.
- Security: no outbound connections observed during a 30-minute baseline run; all TLS certs verified against provided CA.

Operational considerations and runbook items:
- Backup/restore for control plane DB (Postgres snapshot + wal-gcs style export but kept in on-prem object store).
- Telemetry: optional push to internal metrics gateway via proxy; if not allowed, ensure local Prometheus + Grafana bundle for POC.
- Software upgrades: offline patch process documented; ability to roll back to previous image via manifest.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Kubernetes version mismatch -> Mitigate: Offer single-node managed runtime for POC or help schedule safe upgrade window.
- Risk: HSM integration delays -> Mitigate: temporary soft-KMS with strict audit and plan to swap to HSM post-POC.
- Risk: SELinux/AppArmor blocking -> Mitigate: provide policy snippets and test harness early in staging.

Open questions for customer (to resolve prior to install):
- Which registry hosting option preferred for air-gap? (Nexus/Artifactory/Harbor on-site)
- Will customer provide an internal package repository for RPM/DEB?
- KMS integration: prefer direct PKCS#11 or HSM gateway?
- Maintenance window constraints for the real cluster upgrade.
- Compliance export rules for logs/metrics (any PII scrubbing needed?).

Workshop agenda (1.5 hours suggested)
- 00:00-00:10: Introductions + success criteria (Ava / Diego)
- 00:10-00:25: Customer environment walkthrough (network, infra, ops)
- 00:25-00:45: Installer and air-gap packaging overview (Priya)
- 00:45-01:00: KMS/HSM and secrets discussion (Liam)
- 01:00-01:15: Verification tests and SLOs for POC
- 01:15-01:30: Open questions, immediate next steps and owners

Immediate next steps (owner tags):
- Ava: prepare air-gap image manifest + offline installer (lab test) by 2025-10-21.
- Diego: draft SELinux policy snippets and container runtime checklist by 2025-10-18.
- Priya: create runbooks for KMS soft-mode and HSM swap by 2025-10-20.
- Customer action: provide network diagram and package hosting choice by 2025-10-19.

Appendix: quick commands (air-gap image import examples)
- on staging host: ctr -n k8s.io images import redwood-control-plane-images.tar.gz
- helm --kubeconfig /path/to/kubeconfig install redwood ./chart --set imagePullPolicy=IfNotPresent
- verify: kubectl -n redwood get pods -o wide

Notes to self: keep this doc minimal and move finalized install steps to confluence page CONF-3141 once POC completes. Capture any SELinux denials to a shared gist for troubleshooting.

End of notes.
